rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 8 (base_speed 0.9, otherwise iteration 7) is the best raced design at 85.47, up from 38.64. Progress rose on every track: oval 0.268 (one finish in 20 trials), s-bend 0.160 (from 0.052), slalom 0.113 (from 0.108). Line loss is now zero on all tracks. The speed cut therefore helped progress much more than the earlier 1.4 to 1.1 test suggested. However, max_error is still at the limit: oval 0.0607, s-bend 0.0606, slalom 0.065. Every trial still ends off_track. Across iterations 0 to 8, max_error has stayed pinned at 0.060 to 0.065 under changes to kp, kd, ki, sensor size, span, speed and y. The evaluator's contingency for this case (max_error at or above 0.061 at base_speed 0.9) is to move to geometry and test wheel_track, which has never been varied.

Change. I keep iteration 8 unchanged except geometry.wheel_track, raised from 0.12 to 0.14 m. The track sets how much the fixed left/right motor mismatch turns the robot: turn rate is (vR - vL)/wheel_track, so a wider track gives a smaller turn rate for the same wheel difference. A constant mismatch bias should therefore produce a smaller drift, which fits a max_error pinned just above 0.06. The cost is weaker steering authority on tight bends, which could hurt slalom. The evaluator also allowed 0.10 as the other option. I chose 0.14 because the pinned, track-independent excursion looks like a constant bias rather than a bend-limited error. If max_error rises or slalom progress falls, the next test is 0.10.

Expected result. max_error drops toward or below 0.060 on at least oval and s-bend, with progress holding near the iteration-8 values (oval 0.268, s-bend 0.160, slalom 0.113). Risk: a wider track lowers steering responsiveness, which could cut slalom progress or raise max_error on bends.

Hypotheses. H1: the constant motor-mismatch bias drives the excursion, so a wider track reduces max_error below 0.06. H2: max_error stays at 0.061 or higher with wheel_track 0.14, which would point to sensor geometry or the start transient rather than the drivetrain. Measurements wanted: max_error, line_loss_events and progress per track, plus steering_oscillation to check whether the change in turn scaling adds jitter.
